title: Sprint-to-Scale Governor & Metrics Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This sheet is a compact, operational playbook for moving a feature from pre-launch through staged traffic to full scale while tracking the critical KPIs that indicate health, signal rollback, or indicate further optimization is needed. It is intended for product-ops partnering with SRE, serving-runtime, and product managers.

How to use:
- Owner (PM/product-ops) fills target rows prior to kickoff.
- Engineers/SRE update live measurements during canary and ramp windows.
- On each daily stand during rollout, update the status column and attach any incident links.
- After reaching full ramp, convert the sheet into the quarterly optimization backlog.

1) Executive goals (summary)
- Primary goal: Reach 95% of expected throughput under peak load at <= 1.2x baseline p99 latency within 7 days of ramp without error-rate growth > 0.05%
- Secondary goal: Token cost per 1k requests not exceed budgeted delta of +8% after optimization
- Safety: No customer-facing errors affecting >1% of active sessions in any 24h window.

2) Metric table (columns)
Row headers: metric_name | owner | target | baseline | current | measurement_window | threshold_action | notes | last_updated | jira_link
Sample rows (comma separated for each row):
- successful_requests_pct, SRE (Diego Ruiz), >=99.90%, 99.98%, 99.96%, 1h, alert + pause canary if <99.8% for 30m, includes 5xx and 429, 2026-02-20, PRODOPS-487
- p99_latency_ms, Serving Runtime (Maya Patel), <=220ms, 180ms, 205ms, 1h, scale pool / enable smaller batch-policy if >300ms for 15m, measured at ingress-edge, 2026-02-20, PRODOPS-489
- token_cost_per_1k, Product Ops (Avery Chen), <=$3.20, $2.95, $3.10, 24h, cost-review + quantization experiment if > +12% from baseline, includes caching savings, 2026-02-19, PRODOPS-500
- regen_rate_pct (retries due to hallucination), QA (Priya Narayanan), <=2.0%, 0.8%, 1.1%, 24h, run additional prompt-safety eval if >3%, tied to quality eval cohort A, 2026-02-18, PRODOPS-512

3) Canary schedule (recommended defaults)
- Window 0 (initial): 0-5% traffic for 60 minutes. OBSERVE metrics. No code changes.
- Window 1 (extended canary): 5-20% traffic for 3 hours if Window 0 stable. Daily on-call review.
- Window 2 (ramp): 20-50% over 24 hours with checkpoints at 20%, 35%, 50%.
- Window 3 (scale): 50-100% over 48 hours with performance tuning in parallel.
- Emergency pause: immediate pause + rollback to last known-good model/variant if any threshold_action triggers.

4) Acceptance gates (checklist)
- [ ] Preflight: integration tests green (suite: canary-integration-v2) — owner: eng-release, due: T-2d
- [ ] Preflight: load test at 1.2x expected peak passed — owner: perf-team, due: T-2d
- [ ] Security review complete (KMS + audit logs) — owner: security, due: T-1d
- [ ] Observability hooks added (traces, per-route cost) — owner: observability, due: T-1d
- [ ] Rollback artifact created and smoke-tested — owner: release-engineering, due: T-1d
- [ ] Customer comms draft and beta cohort list ready — owner: customer-success, due: T-1d

5) Threshold actions (quick reference)
- If p99_latency >= 300ms for 15m -> auto-scale GPU pool + change batch_policy to latency-first; notify on-call and PM.
- If successful_requests_pct < 99.8% for 30m -> pause canary (stop routing new traffic), rollback to previous variant if immediate improvement not seen in 20m.
- If error-rate spike concentrated in one region -> route traffic away from region until mitigated.
- If token_cost_per_1k > target by +15% sustained for 24h -> revert aggressive model variant and open cost-optimization ticket.

6) Incident triage template (copy this into incident doc)
- Time observed: 
- Impacted customers: 
- Symptoms: (latency | 5xx | incorrect outputs | cost spike)
- Immediate mitigation taken: 
- Root cause hypothesis: 
- Actions to stabilize: (short-term) 
- Long-term follow-ups and owners: 
- Postmortem owner & due date: 

7) Runway and dependencies (roadmap table)
Columns: milestone | owner | eta | blockers | acceptance_criteria
- Preflight tests automated, eng-release, 2026-02-28, flaky perf harness, all tests passing >95%
- Canary rollout plan approved, product-ops, 2026-03-03, SRE staffing gap, documented canary checklist and rollback steps
- Cost optimization experiments queued, product-ops, 2026-03-10, quantization infra ready, experiment tickets linked

8) Communication plan (who notifies who and when)
- Day 0: Announcement to internal #release and #oncall channels; include runbook link. Owner: PM
- During canary: hourly checkpoint posts to #release until 50% traffic. Owner: product-ops
- Post-ramp: 1-day postmortem notes and metrics snapshot to execs. Owner: Head of Product Ops

9) Acceptance signoff (for go/no-go)
Fields for signoff line: role | name | approval (yes/no) | notes | timestamp
- PM | Avery Chen |  |  | 
- Eng Lead | Maya Patel |  |  | 
- SRE Lead | Diego Ruiz |  |  | 
- Security | Liam O'Connor |  |  | 
- Customer Success | Priya Narayanan |  |  | 

10) Post-launch checkpoints (30/60/90 days)
- Day 30: stability check (p99, error rate, cost) -> owner: product-ops
- Day 60: optimization window (apply model quantization / batching config) -> owner: optimize team
- Day 90: retrospective + convert unresolved work into roadmap tickets -> owner: product-ops

Notes to reviewers / TODOs:
- Need a short script to pull these KPIs from metrics API into this sheet every hour; ticket queued (PRODOPS-532).
- Add a small column for ‘observed_anomaly_tag’ to help automated postmortem grouping.
- Consider adding a lightweight quality-eval cohort (50 prompts) to run every ramp step to detect semantic regressions.

Change log:
- 2025-11-03 Avery Chen: created initial draft with metric table and canary schedule.
- 2025-11-18 Maya Patel: added latency thresholds and batch-policy recommendations.
- 2026-01-10 Diego Ruiz: inserted incident triage template and communication plan.
- 2026-02-20 Priya Narayanan: updated regeneration/quality metric and post-launch checkpoints.

Attachments and quick links (paste relevant artifacts into sheet):
- load-test results (s3://redwood-perf/loadtests/2026-02-15)
- canary runbook doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PROD/Canary+Runbooks
- eval set (quality cohort A): gs://redwood-evals/cohortA/2026-02-01.json

If you are using this for an upcoming launch, tag @product-ops on the document and paste the canary schedule under the Jira ticket assigned to the rollout.
